'''''Primula algida''''' is a species of [[flowering plant]] within the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] [[Primulaceae]].<ref>Hassler M. (2019). World Plants: Synonymic Checklists of the Vascular Plants of the World (version Nov 2018). In: Species 2000 & ITIS Catalog of Life, 2019 Annual Checklist (Roskov Y., Ower G., Orrell T., Nicolson D., Bailly N., Kirk PM, Bourgoin T., DeWalt RE, Decock W., Nieukerken E van, Zarucchi J., Penev L., eds.). Digital resource at www.catalogueoflife.org/annual-checklist/2019. Species 2000: Naturalis, Leiden, the Netherlands. ISSN 2405-884X.</ref> This species was first described by [[Johann Friedrich Adam|Michael Friedrich Adams]].<ref>Adams (1805), In: Weber & Mohr, Beitr. 1: 46</ref>

== Description ==
''Primula algida'' is a [[Perennial plant|perennial]] species. Leaves are elliptic and grow from 1 – 6 cm long. The plant can grow from 3 – 20 cm tall when in flower due to its stem.<ref name=":0">{{cite POWO |id=701520-1 |title=''Primula algida'' |accessdate=16 March 2022}}</ref> Each stem holds 4 or more flowers, which can range in colour from mauve to violet.<ref name=":1">{{cite web |url=http://encyclopaedia.alpinegardensociety.net/plants/Primula/algida |title=Home |website=encyclopaedia.alpinegardensociety.net |access-date=2022-03-16}}</ref> The roots of this species are thin and white.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-03-19 |title=Flora of Pakistan Primula algida |url=http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=5&taxon_id=200017139 |website=efloras.org}}</ref>

== Distribution ==
The [[Native species|native]] range of ''P. algida'' includes: [[Caucasus]], Northern [[Northern Iran|Iran]], Northern [[Altai Republic]], [[Mongolia]], [[Pamir-Alay]] and [[Afghanistan]].<ref name=":0" />

== Habitat ==
''Primula algida'' grows on moist ground among grasses in [[Alpine climate|alpine]] areas and [[wet meadow]]s.<ref name=":2">{{inaturalist taxon|557051|''Primula algida''}}</ref>

It also inhabits south facing rock ledges, cliffs and slopes.<ref name=":2" />

This species is found at elevations between 2000-7000m.<ref name=":1" />
